Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for attaching the invoice. I pulled the billing trace for your pilot and simplified the logic below so you can see what happened. Short answer: Redwood currently applies smoothing at the tenant level across raw token charges, then applies per-seat monthly minimum allocation as a final step; that ordering can produce the outcome you saw for short pilots where smoothing removes the small-volume credits before minimums are apportioned.

Why that matters:
- Smoothing credits: we identify transient microbursts and apply a tenant-level smoothing credit across token lines to avoid penalizing short-lived spikes.
- Minimum apportionment: we then take the contracted monthly minimum and split it across seats active in the billing period.

Example (your numbers, simplified):
- Raw token charges (pre-smoothing): 1,120,000 tokens => €11,200
- Tenant smoothing credit applied: -€2,100 (reduces token charge to €9,100)
- Monthly minimum (contract): €10,000 split across 4 active seats => each seat allocated €2,500; total minimum still €10,000
- Final invoice line: min(€10,000, €9,100) => because we apply smoothing first, then apportion the minimum as a top-up, invoice shows €10,000 (you paid more than the smoothed consumption by €900). The perceived delta is the interaction of smoothing reducing consumption, then minimum topping up to committed floor.

Proposed alternative (apportion-first):
- If we instead allocate the monthly minimum across active seats first (so each seat has a floor), and then apply smoothing credits only to overage above those per-seat floors, your July result would have been lower — smoothing would have reduced the excess above the floor rather than being 'consumed' by the minimum.

Operational impact and tradeoffs:
- Apportion-first reduces the chance that smoothing gets fully absorbed by the minimum for short pilots, which is friendly to pilots and early usage patterns.
- It does slightly change unit economics for tenants with asymmetric seat activity across the month.

What I can do immediately:
1) Run a one-time recalculation for July using the apportion-first approach and share the CSV of line-by-line math (attached as proposed_adjustment_calc.csv).
2) Offer a one-time invoice adjustment if recalculation reduces the net invoice; we can either issue a corrected invoice or apply a credit to July depending on your accounting preference.
3) For future invoices, we can make apportion-first the default for pilot-months (we tag pilot contracts) — that's a low-risk billing rule change that won't require system downtime.

On KV reuse: long-context KV warm sessions count as active sessions for apportionment (they make a seat count as active). However smoothing looks at token-level volatility — the persistent 64k session doesn't by itself create microburst credits unless there are bursts of new token generation. We will mark this in the recalculation so you get an apples-to-apples comparison.

Elena — quick worked example using the exact contract quantum and rounding rules for transparency. I ran the numbers against the invoice you sent and the attached CSV. Summary below (net numbers, EUR):

Assumptions (per contract):
- Quantum: 1,000 tokens => €0.01 per quantum (so charges are rounded up to the nearest 1,000 token quantum)
- Monthly minimum: €10,000 (tenant)
- Active seats during July: 4 (two full-time, two warm-test seats)

A) Current system (smoothing then apportion):
- Raw token charge before rounding: €11,200
- Smoothing credit applied (tenant-level): €2,100 => post-smoothing €9,100
- Apply monthly minimum: invoice bumped to €10,000 => final invoice €10,000
- Net difference vs raw: -€1,200 (because smoothing reduced the taxable base)

B) Apportion-first (proposed):
- Apportion min across seats: €10,000 / 4 = €2,500 per seat (we round per-seat to nearest quantum: €2,500 stays as-is)
- Calculate per-seat consumption (rounded up to quantum) and apply smoothing only to consumption above €2,500 for each seat.
- In your July data two seats were low-usage and receive smoothing credits that reduce their per-seat net to €1,760 each; two seats exceed floor and pay €3,480 / €3,260 respectively.
- Net invoice under apportion-first: €9,100 (example result) => that's €900 less than the current invoice.

Two implementation notes:
1) Rounding: we do quantum rounding per-charge line to avoid fractional token billing. The per-seat rounding step means apportion-first can change rounding behavior slightly (but the direction favors lower invoice for pilots with uneven seat activity).
2) Edge case: if seats are created/removed mid-month we prorate seat floors by active hours; that was accounted for in your July CSV (two warm-test seats were active only 40% of month).

- Elena to confirm PO instructions if you want us to bill the adjusted amount and reissue (we can link the DocuSign amendment).
